samples.summary: Requiring EVERY CI run for a SHA to be green makes a superseded red run permanently block promotion, and the harness's own recovery path cannot clear it
samples.evidence:
`ciConclusion` returns "failure" if `!runs.every(r => r.conclusion === "success")`. The docstring justifies this with "a re-run does not create a second run" — true for re-runs, but NOT for re-*triggers* of the same SHA. `ci.yml` has `pull_request: branches: [main]` with default activity types, which include `reopened`: closing and reopening a PR, or force-pushing a branch back to a SHA that was already tested, produces a SECOND CI run for the same head_sha while the first (possibly red) run still exists. The deleted test `gate 1 reads the NEWEST CI run` asserted exactly the case that now regresses ("a re-run that went green supersedes the red run it replaced").

The stall is not self-healing: the two recovery affordances in the repo, `agent-loop.yml:142-146` and `agent-rerun.yml:186-190`, both call `listWorkflowRuns({ workflow_id: 'ci.yml', head_sha, per_page: 1 })` and re-run only `workflow_runs[0]` — i.e. only ONE of the SHA's CI runs. So `@claude loop` / `@claude rerun` cannot turn the stale red run green, `ciPassed` (mark-ready.mjs:136) keeps returning false, mark-ready exits 1, and the promote job logs "leaving as draft" and SUCCEEDS. That is precisely the "a PR that should have merged would sit as a draft forever" failure the comment at agent-review-panel.yml:1444-1452 exists to prevent. Recovery requires a human to find and re-run the older run in the Actions UI, and the new loop-status note ("a ready gate was not satisfied") gives no hint that this is the cause.

samples.summary: `split("@")[0]` re-opens the forgeability hole the path match was added to close
samples.evidence: `ciRunsFor` compares `String(r?.path ?? "").split("@")[0]` against `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. The stated invariant (checks.mjs:54-56) is "only one file can occupy it, so a run's path names the file that produced it". Truncating at the first `@` breaks that one-to-one mapping: `@` is a legal character in a git path, so a second workflow file at `.github/workflows/ci.yml@anything.yml` (still a `.yml` file, so GitHub will load and run it) reports `path` = `.github/workflows/ci.yml@anything.yml`, which this predicate truncates to the real CI path and accepts as CI. The gate then reads that file's green conclusion as "the tests passed" — the exact substitution the change was made to prevent, and one `checks.test.mjs`'s `pwn.yml` case does not cover. The `@ref` suffix the truncation exists for is speculative anyway: a `workflow_call`ed workflow does not produce its own run, so no run in this repo's data actually carries the suffix (the tests assert it only against synthetic fixtures).

samples.summary: Matching on `path` instead of `name` fails closed to a total, silent stall if `path` is ever absent from a run object
samples.evidence: `ciRunsFor` requires `r.path` to match exactly; `checks.test.mjs:447` pins that a run with no `path` is not CI. `checkPassed`'s old discriminator (`r.name`) is a field the API always populates, whereas `path` was added later and is dropped by any trimmed/partial response. If it is missing (or if `ci.yml` is ever renamed — the new `checks.test.mjs` test only proves the file exists, not that it is the file whose runs the API reports), `ciConclusion` returns `null` for every SHA, gate 1 becomes unsatisfiable for every PR, and mark-ready exits 1 with the benign "leaving as draft" message. Fail-closed, but a repo-wide, silent promotion stall rather than a loud error.
searchedFor: grep for workflow_runs consumers in .github/workflows and scripts

samples.summary: `cat` under `set -e` can abort the gate step before the `case` records any `outcome`, so a real tooling failure is reported as "cancelled, killed, or never ran"
samples.evidence: `set -e` is restored at line 1502, then line 1503 runs `cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/mark-ready.log"` before the `case`. If the log was never created — e.g. `RUNNER_TEMP` unset or unwritable, so the `>` redirection at line 1500 itself failed — `cat` exits non-zero and `set -e` terminates the step immediately, so no branch of the new `case` runs and no `outcome=` is written. `$code` (the real signal) is discarded. The loop-status step then falls into the `*)` arm at line 1569 and tells the human the gate "was cancelled, killed, or never ran" when in fact it ran and failed on its own scaffolding — the mis-attribution the block's own comment (lines 1508-1514) says it exists to eliminate.

verdict.reason: Every element of the finding checks out in the repo. checks.mjs:88 does require `runs.every(r => r.conclusion === "success")` over ALL ci.yml runs for a head SHA, with no newest-wins tie-break (tests at checks.test.mjs:456-457 lock this in). ci.yml:9-10 uses `pull_request: branches: ["main"]` with no `types:` filter (default types include `reopened`) and ci.yml has no `concurrency:` block at all, so a second CI run record for the same head_sha is genuinely producible (reopen, or two PRs sharing a head commit) while the earlier red/cancelled record survives. mark-ready.mjs:129 queries runs repo-wide by head_sha and ciRunsFor (checks.mjs:61-63) admits both, so ciPassed (mark-ready.mjs:136,139) returns false permanently and gate 1 (mark-ready.mjs:166) fails. Both recovery affordances — agent-loop.yml:142-146 and agent-rerun.yml:186-190 — call listWorkflowRuns with per_page: 1 and re-run only workflow_runs[0], so neither can clear the older stale run; agent-iterate-ci's red arm is workflow_run-event driven and does not re-fire for a superseded run. The promote job then exits 1 / "leaving as draft" and SUCCEEDS, which is exactly the "sit as a draft forever" liveness failure the comment at agent-review-panel.yml:1448-1452 exists to prevent. No guard makes this unreachable; it is a real correctness/liveness bug on a normal-use path, major severity.

"").split("@")[0] === CI_WORKFLOW_PATH`, while checks.mjs:54-56 states the load-bearing invariant that "only one file can occupy [the path], so a run's path names the file that produced it". Truncating at the first `@` breaks that mapping — `@` is legal in a git path, so a second `.yml` file at `.github/workflows/ci.yml@anything.yml` reports a `path` that this predicate maps onto the real CI path. finding.summary: gate 1's "newest CI run wins" rule (now pinned by the new test) can fail open when a SHA has more than one CI run
finding.evidence: `ciPassed` (mark-ready.mjs:133-137) filters to runs named "CI", sorts by `created_at` descending and returns `runs[0].conclusion === "success"`, ignoring every other CI run for the SHA. The new test (mark-ready.test.mjs:211-247) enshrines this as the intended semantics via fabricated fixtures where a re-run has a later `created_at`. In the real Actions API a re-run does NOT create a new workflow run — it adds a `run_attempt` to the existing run, keeping `created_at` — so the only way a single SHA has two CI runs is when CI is triggered twice for it (e.g. push + pull_request, or a workflow_dispatch alongside), and in that case a RED CI run for the head SHA is silently ignored whenever a differently-triggered CI run created later is green. Gate 1 is the "the tests passed" gate, so this promotes a PR whose CI is not entirely green. Reading the newest run is also nondeterministic if `created_at` is absent/invalid on any run (`new Date(undefined)` → NaN comparator → unspecified sort order), and there is no `status === "completed"` check, so an in-flight later attempt is judged on a stale conclusion field.

verdict.reason: The described code is not present in this working tree. mark-ready.mjs:125-137 `ciPassed` contains no name filter, no `created_at` sort and no `runs[0]` — it delegates to `ciConclusion(data.workflow_runs)`. checks.mjs:61-63 filters CI runs by workflow PATH, and checks.mjs:84-89 implements the exact opposite of "newest wins": it returns null when no run exists, null when ANY run has `conclusion == null` (the in-flight guard the finding says is missing), and otherwise requires `runs.every(r => r.conclusion === "success")`, so a red CI run for the SHA yields "failure" regardless of ordering. Because no timestamp comparator is used, the claimed NaN/unspecified-sort nondeterminism cannot arise. The test cited as enshrining newest-wins (mark-ready.test.mjs:258-304) asserts the reverse semantics with identical `created_at` on both runs: exit 1 for success+failure in both orders, exit 1 for green+in-flight(null), exit 0 only when both are green; and mark-ready.test.mjs:211-247 is the path-filter/forgery test, not a re-run timestamp fixture. The newest-wins pattern the finding quotes survives only in the baseline copy (.trusted/scripts/agent/set-state.mjs:226), i.e. the branch under review is the fix for it.
